name: Date night
blurb: Something worth sitting down for, without spending the evening at the hob.
tip: Cook one thing properly rather than three things at once. Lay the table before you start.

name: Movie night
blurb: Eaten on a lap, made mostly in advance, nothing that needs a knife and fork battle.
tip: Anything you can eat one handed wins. Get it finished before the film starts, not during.

name: Family together
blurb: One pot, everyone served at once, enough for seconds.
tip: Put it in the middle of the table and let people serve themselves. It changes the meal.

name: I don’t know what I want
blurb: Somewhere you have not eaten before, chosen for you.
tip: Pick the one that sounds strangest. That is usually the good decision.

name: Friends coming over
blurb: Scales up easily, most of it done before anyone arrives.
tip: Choose something that sits happily for twenty minutes. Guests are never on time.

name: Just me
blurb: Small, quick, no leftovers you will resent on Thursday.
tip: Cooking for one is still cooking. Use a plate.

name: Cook once, eat twice
blurb: Better on the second day, freezes without complaint.
tip: Cool it quickly, then fridge or freeze. Most stews improve overnight.

name: Too tired to cook
blurb: Fifteen minutes, one pan, nothing to think about.
tip: Low effort is not a failure. Eating something decent beats not eating.
